note: No parcel identifiers. Future concept on the east land.

slopes.notes: Positive percent is rising in the direction of the transect. The parcel faces north: ground falls toward Deal Rd and rises toward the south woods.

access_public.deal_rd: Deal Rd runs east-west about 900+ ft north of the house. The existing driveway comes in from the north and curves down the west side to the west-facing garage.
access_public.east_land_frontage: The east land does not have its own Deal Rd frontage. Recommended access is a spur off the existing driveway, past the gym barn, with a turnaround at the cottage.
access_public.track: An unpaved track east of the house heads toward a neighbor and other roads; it is probably not this land’s road frontage.

cottage_public.siting: Southeast of the gym barn, on the east land, clear of both barns. Uphill and south of the main house so it sits out of the primary north/lake view from the wrap deck. The gym barn plus a new evergreen (or mixed) buffer on the cottage’s north-west side screens the main house’s east deck. Porch faces north / north-east, looking down the falling grade toward distant Elk Lake.
cottage_public.screening: Propose a 2–3 row evergreen (or mixed native) buffer on the NW side, 20–30 ft deep, and keep existing south-edge trees. A low berm (3–4 ft) can be added if, after leaf-off, the east deck still sees the cottage.
cottage_public.confidence: Moderate. Bare-earth 2016 1 m 3DEP is reliable for grade; it does not include trees or buildings. Leaf-on aerials show woods west/south/north of the house and a mostly open field on the east land, with more trees at the south edge — good for screening a SE cottage, but winter views may be more open. Distant lake views are elevated, not shoreline. Intervening vegetation between here and the lake is not modeled. Confirm on site, preferably leaf-off.

sauna.spot: Keep the 8×12 wood-fired sauna just east of the inset east deck, on piers if the local grade needs them, with the cold plunge on the deck.
sauna.note: The steep drop at this house is to the NORTH (walk-out under the wrap deck), not a sharp east-facing bluff. The east side is a milder cross-slope; piers are still reasonable if the yard falls away at the deck edge or over the east yard. Measure on site before building the pier foundation.

lake_views.direction: Elk Lake water is about 1.5 km or more to the east / northeast of the house (not a backyard shoreline). “Lake views north” from the wrap deck and from a north-facing cottage porch are distant, elevated views, more NNE/NE than due north.

driveway_costs_estimates.label: ESTIMATES only, Northern Michigan ballpark, not bids. A separate driveway/contractor quote should replace these.
driveway_costs_estimates.fire_notes: If the spur is a dead end longer than about 150 ft, many fire codes (IFC Appendix D / local rural standards) want a turnaround (hammerhead or T) and often a 20-ft unobstructed width. Confirm with Whitewater Township and the fire department. Grades on the spur should stay under ~10% if possible.

utilities_public.disclaimer: Approximate, from the 1993 sketch, not surveyed.
utilities_public.existing: Well north of the house; 2,000-gal tank about 22 ft south of the house; 21×50 ft drain bed about 22 ft beyond the tank (no-drive / no-build); house-to-tank sewer; 50 ft well setback and 10 ft property-line setback.
utilities_public.optionA: Tie the barn bath into the house water and septic, about $15K–$42K plus possible septic enlargement. A direct trench would cut the drain field — route around it. Permits required. Accessory use only.
utilities_public.optionB: Future option: separate well and septic near the rear barn. Well $10K–$20K, septic $10K–$25K, bath build-out $10K–$20K, total about $30K–$65K. The well could also serve a future cottage. Accessory use only (no bedroom or kitchen). Estimates; permits required.
